latest_final: A man murdered his romantic partner. To keep suspicion away from himself, he wants it believed she is still alive and has simply gone away for good—so he is faking a farewell note in her handwriting, written as if she were addressing him: "You've disappointed me so much; I'm never coming back." Because it must pass as hers, he practices that sentence over and over on paper, disguising his own hand to imitate her script. The repeated identical lines are these forging attempts. But each attempt is still recognizably his own handwriting, not hers, so he cannot make the forgery convincing. His sigh—"I know I'm in trouble"—means he senses the plan is failing and that these leftover practice sheets, in his own telltale hand, will incriminate him as her killer.
